transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... I guess I'm here because I keep forgetting things. Things I really shouldn't be forgetting. 

Like... follow-up appointments for my heart. Or calling the clinic back when I'm supposed to. Even just... going to do a repair job and realizing I didn't bring the right tools. 

So... yeah. That's mostly it.
Did this problem with forgetting things start suddenly or did it come on gradually over time?

Well... I guess it's been causing real trouble for about a year and two months now. 

It wasn't exactly sudden, but it got worse after my cardiac scare. I had to... cut back on all the walking I was doing. And my projects. I used to rely on those things to just... keep me settled, I suppose. 

So without them... yeah. About a year and a couple months.
Do you have trouble focusing or paying attention to things?

I suppose I do. Like... if I sit down at the bridge table, or a Fix-It Friends planning meeting. 

I mean to pay close attention, but... after a little while, my mind just sort of slides off. I'll realize I missed half of what was said. So... yes.
Do you ever find it hard to express your thoughts in a coherent and logical way?
No, I don't think so. I can... get my point across fine. When I need to.
Do you ever feel confused about where you are or what's going on around you?
No... I don't have that problem. I always know where I am.
Do you ever feel disoriented or unsure about the date or time?
No. I know what day it is. I keep track of the time just fine.
Have you noticed any difficulty remembering how to do things you've learned to do in the past, like hobbies or work-related skills?
No... I still know how to do things. That hasn't been a problem.
Do you have trouble remembering things that happened recently, like what you did yesterday or last week?
No, I remember things fine. Yesterday... last week, it's all there. Memory isn't the issue.
Do you have trouble learning new information?
No, I can learn things alright. It's just... I don't really sit still long enough for much of that, but the learning part is fine.
Do you think your forgetfulness is because you're not paying attention when people tell you things or when you're supposed to do them?

I suppose so. It's not that I don't try to listen. I'll sit down at the bridge table, or... a Fix-It Friends planning meeting, meaning to pay close attention. But after a little while, my mind just sort of slides off. Then I realize I missed half of what was said. So... yeah, probably.
Do you think your mind slides off because you're distracted by something else or because you're just having trouble staying focused?

I guess it's distractions. It doesn't take much. If somebody coughs... or a chair scrapes... I lose my place. Even just seeing someone walk past the window at the senior center. I'm off looking at that instead of the repair list, or... the card game.
Do you think you would remember things better if you were in a quieter, less distracting environment?
I don't know. Maybe. I haven't really thought about it.
Do you think you would be able to remember things if someone reminded you or helped you stay on track?
Hard to say. I don't really have anyone... checking up on me like that to keep me on track. So I couldn't tell you if it would work or not.
Do you think you would remember instructions or tasks if you wrote them down?
I... I don't know. I guess I could try that. I don't really carry a notepad around, though.
Do you think you would remember things better if someone directly told them to you, rather than you having to pay attention to them in a conversation?
I don't really know. I suppose... maybe? It's hard to say if that would really make much of a difference. I haven't really noticed.
Do you think you would be able to recall the information if someone repeated it back to you immediately after you forgot it?
Could be. I mean... if they just said it again right then, maybe it would stick. But I really couldn't say for sure. I haven't paid much attention to that.
Do you think you would remember things if you were able to focus your attention on them without any distractions?
Hard to say. I guess... maybe. But there's always something going on around me, so I don't really know. I couldn't tell you for sure.
Do you think you would remember things if you were able to focus on them at the moment they were told to you?
I'm not really sure. I suppose... if I was focused right then, maybe. But I just haven't thought about it like that. It's hard to tell.
Do you think you would remember things if you were able to give them your full attention when they were first told to you?
Like I said... I really don't have a good answer for you on that. I guess it's possible. But I just don't keep track of how all that works, so I couldn't tell you either way.
Do you think you would be able to remember things if you were in a setting where nothing else was competing for your attention?
Look, it's... it's like I've been saying. I just don't know. I've never really been anywhere where absolutely nothing is going on. So... I just can't give you a straight answer on that.
